I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest way for me to use my 10.9 mu, my well water, and the labor my family can still put in while some people work off-farm. I do not want to spread myself too thin, so I will put 8.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 2.9 mu in cotton because cotton still gives me a way to spread risk and use my experience. I will use better seed on all three crops because I care more about stable emergence, yield, and disease resistance than saving a little money on seed. I will fertilize wheat more evenly because it responds well and sets up the maize crop after harvest; for maize I will push nitrogen but keep phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels; for cotton I will feed it enough but not too heavily so it does not run too much to stalk. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water at the key stages instead of too often. I will use rotary tillage on the wheat-maize land to save time and labor, and I will plough the cotton ground because I want a deeper loose layer there. I expect wheat and maize to be my main output, and cotton to be a smaller but useful part of the farm.
